articles.title: Sudanese Communist Party demands release of arrested member
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: The Sudanese Communist Party has condemned the arrest of Ahmed Babiker, known as Jughraf, a party member in the South Blue Nile region, and demanded his immediate release or that he be brought before a competent court. In a press statement, the party said Babiker was arrested by the security unit in Ed Damazin on Thursday, November 5, at the Agadi exit checkpoint. He was traveling by motorcycle with a colleague, Haq-Allah, who was not detained and was subsequently released. According to the statement, the two were heading to a camp for internally displaced persons to undertake a construction project. articles.title: Anti-Netanyahu bloc led by Eisenkot tasked with forming new Israeli government
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: Israeli President Isaac Herzog officially tasked the leader of the anti-Netanyahu bloc, led by Gadi Eisenkot, with forming the next government, on Sunday, November 8. This came after Eisenkot secured 67 Knesset recommendations (combining 48 from his own coalition and 19 from Arab-led parties) surpassing the 61-seat threshold needed to form a government. After receiving the mandate, the designated candidate has a 28-day window (plus a potential 14-day extension granted by the Israeli president) to assemble a majority coalition in order to form a government with a minimum of 61 lawmakers. In the meantime, Benjamin Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister until the new government takes office, as per Israel’s Basic Law. articles.title: Spain: From occupation to general strike
articles.author: Thomas Hummel
articles.content_excerpt: W hen the Policía Nacional of Madrid raided María del Carmen Abascal’s home to forcibly remove the 87-year-old from her apartment of over 70 years, they undoubtedly did not expect to kindle a nationwide explosion for dignified housing. The housing company Urbagestión had purchased her property and tripled her rent to more than her entire monthly state pension. As these pigs told the old woman and the protesters who had gathered to defend her that they were “just doing their job,” they certainly did not suspect that this would be the spark that would ignite a hot autumn in Madrid and across all of the Spanish state. articles.title: French unions and students fight on as government offers “crumbs”
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: Nationwide mobilizations against austerity have continued in France following the massive strike on November 5, with additional protests announced for November 10 , 14, 17, and 19. Hundreds of thousands persist in resisting the cuts-based policies envisioned by President Emmanuel Macron and the government of Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu. articles.title: “We Have to Be Brave”: Palestinian Journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh Speaks Out After Israeli Detention
articles.content_excerpt: The prominent journalist Abed Abu Shehadeh, a Palestinian citizen of Israel, has been released from Israeli custody after five days in detention. He was arrested on Wednesday by armed police and Shin Bet agents who conducted a nighttime raid on his home in the Israeli city of Jaffa. Abu Shehadeh’s detention was related to his reporting on the October 27 Israeli election and the role of Palestinian political parties. Ahead of the election, he interviewed Azmi Bishara, a Palestinian intellectual and former member of the Israeli Knesset who has lived in exile in Qatar since fleeing Israel amid allegations that he aided Hezbollah during the 2006 Lebanon war.
